Todo lo que un ordenador «sabe» ahora mi: Everything a computer “knows” right now is stored in circuits like this one. The processor's registers, which is where the numbers it is operating on at this instant live, are rows of flip-flops; and so is the cache memory, the fast and expensive one. Main memory uses another, cheaper and slower technique, a tiny capacitor that keeps discharging and has to be refreshed thousands of times a second, and that difference of technology is exactly why a computer has little fast memory and a lot of slow memory. Metastability is not theoretical either: when two parts of a system run on different clocks, the data crossing from one to the other may catch the flip-flop in mid-hesitation, and that is why two or three are chained in a row to give it time to make up its mind.
